qa_stack.profile: bring the stack up with `docker compose -f compose.yml up -d --build --force-recreate --wait` and drive it over http://localhost:18085; the Firebase Auth emulator comes up beside it on http://localhost:18086 and every token a scenario needs is signed in there. Sandboxed runs reach both through the forwarded ports declared in the book's runbook node (`docs/features/claims/ops/qa-stack.md`)
fixtures: an empty desk (DELETE /api/claims, holding the adjuster's token) so a duplicate-claim scenario decides what is already on file
a signed-in holder (POST accounts:signInWithPassword on the emulator) whose subject the stored claim is attributed to
qa_stack.capable_of_rendering: the claims API against the live ledger, and the auth emulator against the three identities compose seeds into it
qa_stack.notes: there is no client bundle and no secret: the service is a single Go binary and every credential a scenario needs is minted by the emulator beside it. The two refusal arms — a token for another project, and an expired one — cannot be signed in for and are constructed as JWTs the scenario presents
